subject: bug df count found in lavaan 0.5-14

messages.author: 373e56ec89625c50
messages.subject: bug df count found in lavaan 0.5-14
parts:
a student of mine draw my attention to what i think is a potential bug in lavaan 0.5-14. if the following syntax is run
 
low <- '
1.00
 -.25 1.00
 0.11 -.14 1.00
 0.25 -.22 0.21 1.00
 0.18 -.15 0.19 0.53 1.00
 '
 
 SDs <- c(.33, .62, 1, .54, .47)
 
 S <- getCov(low, lower=TRUE, sds=SDs, names=c("RMBI", "FES", "FEQ", "DERS", "SCL"))
 
 model1<-'DERS ~ RMBI + FES + FEQ
          SCL ~ DERS'

suvegFixedTrue <- sem(model1, fixed.x=FALSE, sample.cov=S, sample.nobs=676, mimic='EQS')
summary(suvegFixedTrue, fit.measures=TRUE)
 
on lavaan 0.5-14, under the heading "Model test baseline model" from the fit measures, it reports an incorrect number of degrees of freedom. this is a 5X5 covariance matrix so there are 15 unique elements - 5 baseline variances that become estimated = 10 dfs. lavaan 0.5-14 reports 7dfs.
 
i further confirmed this is a mistake because i haven't upgraded lavaan (i'm still running 0.5-13) and 0.5-13 does report the correct number of dfs, which are 10.
 
at first i thoght it had to do with the fixed.x=FALSE command but i'm now realising that, in lavaan 0.5-14, regardless of whether one sets the argument to TRUE or FALSE nothing changes on the dfs for the baseline model. in lavaan 0.5-13, changing that does either give 10 dfs (what would be expected) or 7 dfs.
 
just doing my part here to help make lavaan better :-)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: bug df count found in lavaan 0.5-14
parts:
On 09/23/2013 03:26 PM, yrosseel wrote:
> On 09/22/2013 11:50 PM, oolve...@gmail.com wrote:
>
>> on lavaan 0.5-14, under the heading "Model test baseline model" from the
>> fit measures, it reports an incorrect number of degrees of freedom. this
>> is a 5X5 covariance matrix so there are 15 unique elements - 5 baseline
>> variances that become estimated = 10 dfs. lavaan 0.5-14 reports 7dfs.

But wait a minute. lavaan 0.5-14 is actually right! df should be 7, not
10. And it should be df=7 both for fixed.x=TRUE and fixed.x=FALSE.

The 'bug' is not in lavaan 0.5-14, but in 0.5-13 (and possibly in
previous versions too). In 0.5-13, df equals 10 ONLY when fixed.x=FALSE,
but it is df=7 when fixed.x=TRUE.

It turns out that this bug was related to the following:

lavaanNames(fit, type="ov.x", group=1)

did not correctly return the list of exogenous variables (in 0.5-13 and
before). This has been corrected in 0.5-14, and as a happy coincidence
also cured the (latent) df bug for the baseline model when we have
exogenous variables and fixed.x=FALSE.

So why is df=7 (and not 10). Because 3 out of the 5 variables are
exogenous. And under the baseline/independence model, we only assume
that all endogenous variables are uncorrelated; we DO allow for
correlations among the exogenous variables.


Yves.

uhmmm... i see. well, now i'm finding this to be a very, very interesting situation. quoting from EQS 6's pdf manual, page #117 under the Independence Model heading:
 
"The chi-square associated with the model of independent or uncorrelated variables is presented first".
 
by quickly inspecting the EQS outputs (even the ones in the manual) it's relatively straightforward to verify that the formula to calculate the degrees of freedom for this model is: number of unique elements in the covariance matrix - the number of elements in the diagonal. so, for the example above, that's 10 dfs because EQS' assumes that the independence/baseline model is a diagonal matrix.
 
HOWEVER...
 
after re-fitting the same model in Mplus i can see that Mplus reports 7 dfs! just as lavaan 0.5-14! so, in this case, the fomula would be the number of unique elements in the covariance matrix - number of elements elements in the diagonal - the number of covariances among exogenous variables.
 
which, therefore, suggests there are actually two different viewpoints of what constitutes an independence/baseline model, Peter Bentler's and Bengt Muthen's.
 
lavaan 0.5-14 didn't have a bug then. it's just using a different definition of what the baseline/independence model is.
 
thanks for pointing that out... makes me wonder what other theoretical distinctions exist between the EQS way of doing things and the Mplus way.

> thanks for pointing that out... makes me wonder what other theoretical
> distinctions exist between the EQS way of doing things and the Mplus way.

There are many, many differences. I often mention this in presentations
(see eg http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/lavaan_IMPS_2013.pdf).

One of the aims of the lavaan project is to 'mimic' all these
differences (well, as many as possible).

In dev 0.5-15, using mimic="EQS" in your example will result in df=10
for the baseline model.

Yves.

I just encountered this same issue. Thanks for clarifying how lavaan defines the baseline model. I noticed also that if I specify exogenous covariances in the model statement, then lavaan uses a model baseline that includes independence of exogenous variables (so I get more degrees of freedom in the baseline model). It makes some sense, but I wasn't expecting it. E.g., mod2 below gives me a baseline model with 10 df, whereas mod1 gives 9. I actually like that I can use this to decide what I want the baseline model to be, but is this supposed to happen? 

mod1 <- '
AA ~ SRL
FG ~ AA + SGG
SGG ~ PGG + AA #-- baseline model has 9 df
'

mod2 <- '
AA ~ SRL
FG ~ AA + SGG
SGG ~ PGG + AA
SRL ~~ PGG  # explicitly specify the covariance between exogenous predictors -- baseline model has 10 df
'

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: bug df count found in lavaan 0.5-14
parts:
On 02/09/2014 09:57 PM, Mijke Rhemtulla wrote:
> I just encountered this same issue. Thanks for clarifying how lavaan
> defines the baseline model. I noticed also that if I specify exogenous
> covariances in the model statement, then lavaan uses a model baseline
> that includes independence of exogenous variables (so I get more degrees
> of freedom in the baseline model). It makes some sense, but I wasn't
> expecting it. E.g., mod2 below gives me a baseline model with 10 df,
> whereas mod1 gives 9. I actually like that I can use this to decide what
> I want the baseline model to be, but is this supposed to happen?
Yes.

> mod1 <- '
> AA ~ SRL
> FG ~ AA + SGG
> SGG ~ PGG + AA #-- baseline model has 9 df
> '

Ok, here we have the 'usual' setting where we have 5 observed variables,
2 of them are exogenous. The total covariance matrix is 5*6/2=15
'datapoints', but we do not count the exogenous variances/covariances
(because they are fixed). Therefore, we only have 15 - 3 = 12
'datapoints'. In the independence model, we only estimate the variances
of the endogenous variables (3 free parameters), but the
variances/covariances of the fixed exogenous variables remain fixed at
their sample values. Hence, we have 12 - 3 = 9 degrees of freedom.

> mod2 <- '
> AA ~ SRL
> FG ~ AA + SGG
> SGG ~ PGG + AA
> SRL ~~ PGG # explicitly specify the covariance between exogenous
> predictors -- baseline model has 10 df
> '

Here, by explicitly adding the covariance between exogenous predictors
(note that you get a warning if you do this), they are 'upgraded' to
random variables. Hence, their variances/covariances are not fixed. We
have now 15 datapoints (instead of 12), and the independence model now
estimates 5 variances (instead of 3), resulting in 15 - 5 = 10 degrees
of freedom...

BTW, lavaan dev 0.5-16 adds a 'baseline.model' argument to the
fitMeasures() function, so that users can specify their own baseline models.

Yves.
